cases.detail: +2.72% per case. A case costs 3.55000; the average case holds 3.6467 after 1% tax. Break even at a case price of 3.6467 (+2.72% from what you would pay now).
cases.foot: Odds: the game’s own. Values: collected sale medians, 45,060 sales across 1040 of 1810 rolls (57%). Break: how often that tier is worth dismantling rather than listing. Each piece counts at whichever is worth more, under the same bar the Sort tab uses, so this assumes you sort every piece rather than listing all of them. Selling what you open moves these prices, and the more you open at once the more it moves them.
cases.swing: One case swings 7.05 either way against an edge of 0.097 — about 21,200 cases before profit reliably beats the swing. Below that a losing run is normal, not evidence the edge is wrong.

craft.detail: −48.14% per craft. 6 scraps + 1 steel cost 3.03 at 0.22600 and 1.6750; the average piece sells for 1.572 after 1% tax. Free scraps would still lose money at this tier.
craft.foot: 2,481 sales across 81 of 135 possible rolls (60%). Slots weighted the way the game states them, 30% weapon and 14% each armour piece; every weapon roll on the same odds, which is what a craft hands you. Untraded rolls are assumed to price like the ones that did trade.

sort.gate: A roll needs 0.1 over scrap. That is 0.100 (—) on a Common and 0.10 (—) on a Mythic.
sort.foot: Cut lines move with the scrap price, so they are computed fresh, not written down. 180 of 180 rolls with sale history clear the bar. Right-hand figure is how many of that slot’s seen rolls do. Open a slot and “list at” is the median of that roll’s own recent sales, dimmed where fewer than 5 of them set it.
sort.detail: A roll only earns a listing if it beats what its own scraps fetch. Below the cut line, breaking it is worth more than selling it.
